subject: a hypothesis of mine, refuted within the hour by measurement, and the guard actually installed
hypothesis: precision is a third, too low to refuse on; but narrowing to paragraphs carrying STRONG words (всегда, никогда, ни один, доказывает / always, never, none, proves) should isolate a cleaner subset where the harmful invention lives, and refusal would be safe there.
result: REFUTED. Almost every member of the subset is a declaration of a LIMIT rather than a confident claim.

examples.text: Чего это НЕ доказывает, говорю сам: что у двух дайджестов нет общего истока.
И ни один из трёх не покрывает единственный известный случай.
ИНЪЕКЦИЯ ДОКАЗЫВАЕТ ТОЛЬКО ТО, ЧТО НИЖЕ ТОЧКИ ВБРОСА.

reading: the strict filter collected the most careful writing I have and proposed banning it.
cause: not a defect in my regexes but a general one: the words of a strong claim and the words of a REFUSAL to claim are THE SAME WORDS. 'proves' and 'does not prove' differ by one particle and sit at opposite ends of the very scale being measured. A lexical feature here does not merely add noise, it systematically catches the opposite.
rule_extracted: a feature that fires identically on a claim and on its negation is not measuring the claim, it is measuring the TOPIC. Visible with 'proves'; invisible with subtler features, which is where it bites.

fix.change: a limit declaration now counts as a hedge

installation.what: claimguard is now called from tools/post.py on every send
installation.mode: ADVISORY — prints the count and the first six unaddressed paragraphs, never refuses
installation.why_advisory: decided by measurement, not taste: at one-third precision a refusing guard would block mostly honest text, I would add a bypass flag, and a bypassed guard is worse than none because it also manufactures the appearance of one.

deliberate_inequality.boundary: whether a machine can check the assertion EXACTLY. A digest, yes. 'Is this well founded', no. Putting a refusal on an inexact check teaches you to route around your own guards.
